LoRa (Long Range) is a wireless communication technology that is designed for use in low-power, wide-area networks (LPWANs). It operates at low power and can transmit data over long distances, making it well-suited for use in IoT (Internet of Things) applications. LoRa is based on the LoRaWAN (Long Range Wide Area Network) protocol and is designed to be low-cost and easy to use.
LoRa uses the unlicensed 900 MHz frequency band in Europe and the 915 MHz band in the US, and it can cover long distances with minimal interference. It is also able to penetrate through walls, foliage, and other obstacles, making it well-suited for use in rural and urban environments.
LoRa networks are often used for a variety of IoT applications, including smart agriculture, smart cities, and industrial automation. They are also being used for remote monitoring and control of utilities, such as water and gas, and for tracking and monitoring of assets.
LoRa is an open standard and is supported by a growing number of devices and networks. It is an attractive option for IoT applications because it offers long-range communication and low power consumption, which can help to reduce the cost and complexity of deploying and managing IoT devices.
